### 🛡️ Codex Security Review · _Automatically triggered_ Here are some automated security review suggestions for this pull request. **Reviewed commit:** `718c22c6ab`
ℹ️ About Codex security reviews in GitHub
This is an experimental Codex feature. Security reviews are triggered when: - You comment "@codex security review" - A regular code review gets triggered (for example, "@codex review" or when a PR is opened), and you’re opted in so security review runs alongside code review Once complete, Codex will leave suggestions, or a comment if no findings are found.

### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/sharpninja/rideaudit/blob/718c22c6abdb59294b71658cabcfdae72df8d17f/deploy/omarchy/ngrok/remote-start.sh#L97-L105 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Verify the stale PID belongs to this ngrok tunnel** The new PID-reuse guard accepts every process whose command line contains `ngrok http`, not specifically the RideAudit process recorded by this state directory. If a stale PID is reused by another ngrok HTTP tunnel, `start_nohup` treats it as the old RideAudit agent and kills it whenever `ngrok.addr` is absent or differs; the stop script uses the same broad predicate. Match the expected backend and config path in `/proc/$pid/cmdline`, or persist a process identity that cannot mistake an unrelated ngrok tunnel for this one. --- https://github.com/sharpninja/rideaudit/blob/718c22c6abdb59294b71658cabcfdae72df8d17f/deploy/octopus/Invoke-RideAuditOctopusRelease.ps1#L186-L190 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Validate the named Octopus target before pinning it** `Wait-RoleTarget` returns a unique exact-name match without checking that it belongs to the requested environment or has `$TargetRole`, and the returned ID is then placed in `SpecificMachineIds`. A stale target with the expected name but an old environment or tag can therefore be selected even though the process step is filtered to the new role, causing the release to fail or skip the intended worker instead of using the valid role match. Octopus documents that specific machines must be in the target environment and that target tags filter which machines run a step; require both conditions before returning the named match. [Octopus deployment API](https://octopus.com/docs/api/deployments), [environment and target-tag behavior](https://octopus.com/docs/best-practices/deployments/environments-and-deployment-targets-and-roles).

### 🛡️ Codex Security Review · _Automatically triggered_

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub> Security: Bind analysis grants to the data they read**

If the case-grant feature is implemented, bind each analysis grant to the resource IDs those RPCs actually query. These ACs scope all operations by `submission_id`, but coverage uses `import_id`, while online-hours and incident requests carry only driver/time/policy fields and read every matching normalized row. A grantee permitted for submission S1 could therefore request a broad incident window and receive trip/score lines from unlisted import S2; the proposed ungranted-submission test cannot express this case. Grant import IDs or define an immutable submission-to-import binding, enforce it at each sink, and test mixed granted/ungranted rows.

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind bearer access to the named grantee**

The bearer option contradicts the required named-grantee check: with no grantee principal, the server can validate possession of the secret but cannot establish that the caller is the counsel or auditor named in the grant. A forwarded or stolen secret would let an arbitrary holder access the records while the required audit entry falsely attributes the use to the named grantee. Either require an authenticated grantee identity or redefine the approved sentence, scope checks, and logs so the capability itself—not a named person—is the grantee.

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Separate UC-RIDE-010 verification from decryption authorization**

The proposed precondition requires a case grant covering UC-RIDE-010's submissions and operation, yet the allowed operations contain only verification/analysis and the grant explicitly cannot authorize the working-copy operation in steps 4-5. In a valid legal-release scenario, no grant can satisfy the precondition for the complete use case; an implementation must either bypass the stated precondition or incorrectly extend the grant across the decryption boundary. Scope the grant precondition only to verification steps 1-3 and give steps 4-5 their own legal-process precondition, or split them into separate use cases.

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Test the grantee and case scope checks**

TR-RIDE-SEC-004 requires the server to check both grantee and case ID on every call, but TEST-RIDE-058 omits wrong-grantee and wrong-case negatives. An implementation that validates submission, operation, expiry, and revocation while ignoring either of those two bindings would pass every listed test, allowing a grant to be replayed by another principal or under another case. Add explicit mismatched-grantee and mismatched-case calls that return `TENANT_ISOLATION` with no data.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify grant-use logging in TEST-RIDE-058**

FR-RIDE-079 requires every grant use to record the grant ID, grantee, operation, and submission ID, but the proposed happy path asserts only that operations pass. The implementation could return all expected results while omitting the audit record—or recording the wrong grantee or submission—and still satisfy TEST-RIDE-058 as written. Add assertions for one correctly attributed log entry per successful granted operation and, if denied attempts are intended to be auditable, specify and test those separately.

The exact candidate sentence says that without a valid grant the driver may still verify or analyze their own submissions, but this unconditional use-case precondition requires the driver to have issued a case grant even though Driver is also a proposed actor. Applied literally, a driver opening their own coverage, hours, incident, or verification flow is blocked until they create an unnecessary grant. Make the precondition conditional on the Grantee path and retain ordinary driver-principal ownership as the alternative authorization path.
